_about: GM plan and position. Never rendered. Prose for beats, quests and roads lives in saga/bible/_gm/arc.md (saga.py arc <id>); this file holds state. Edit through saga.py plan where a command exists; otherwise with Edit, keeping the canonical format (saga.py fmt).
book_question: Who is hollowing the wounded, and can a knight who cannot stand protect anyone?

chapter.question: What is the House for, and can a knight who cannot stand hold its stair?

slots.plan: Dawn after the lid came off. The far cots' keepers were told in the night; at the dawn bell Darrow tells the Prior, who says once that she counted the nights and asks nothing more (c03.7a). Then Hollis, carried, brings Brother Anselm the almoner to the cot, shaking (c03.7b: Hollis went to him in the night, so the man cannot come of his own accord): he carried it down by the stores key, through the old stair door where the House's wine is laid, never the iron-banded one, which is why the flour never showed a mark; a clerk in grey gave it him at the winch-house before the snow, where he takes the House's letters down to the carter each week, a man he never saw kneel; why: his sister Mirren, held at Calden by the Confessors, who write to him in a clerk's hand. The satchel still holds a second one, wrapped in the letters' oilcloth, unplaced; Maelis takes it without a word. Darrow keeps Hollis's hands off the man, by rank.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows who carried it and why, and that the Confessors hold the almoner's sister; he attempts to keep Hollis from breaking the man, and does it by his rank, the first order he has given since the river

slots.plan: Rae comes up the Steps with the cage's letter rather than leave it below: a letter for the almoner from Calden in a clerk's hand, and a lock of hair folded inside it. Marrant's method: the lever, never the blade. Darrow knows the hand: it addressed his brother's letters. Rae, asked where she has seen it, says only that she has seen that hand before, and will not say where. The House's letters did not go down this week; the almoner reads his sister's letter in front of them and does not weep, which is worse. Hollis asks what a captain does with a man who did a terrible thing for love, and nobody answers.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows what Marrant holds over the almoner and whose household wrote the holding; he attempts to get Rae to say where she has seen the hand, and fails

slots.plan: Wren brings Darrow down the kennel ramp, with the stick he refuses, because they have something in common: a grey bitch with a splinted hind leg who has bitten two lay brothers and the farrier, will not eat, and sleeps against the door that faces the infirmary. The kennel-master wants her put down before the grey cloaks come up and see what the Menders feed. The snarling stops when Darrow sits down on the straw with one hand out, the other's fingertips still wrapped; she puts the splinted leg across his boot and goes to sleep. The kennel-master gives him until the grey cloaks are gone to prove she is worth the feed.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow has a hound's weight on his boot and a kennel-master's deadline; he attempts to sit still with a dog that bites, and she chooses him

slots.plan: Dusk at the bars. Marrant, courteous to the whole court, asks after the House's almoner by name: the letters have not come down this week, and a woman in Calden is waiting on her brother's reply. He names a price pleasantly: the almoner's name, and two others come off the list. The Prior, beside Darrow this time, says the law of guests covers a brother of the House; Marrant thanks her for it. Wren counts the grey cloaks at the fires: one fewer than yesterday. Inside, with Anselm, Hollis, Maelis and Wren at the cot, what the House is for: the beat choice.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow knows Marrant's price and that the lever is the whole of his method; he must decide what the House is for and attempts to buy a night first, which the Prior pays for

micro.ask: What does Darrow do with the almoner?
options: Expose him to the Prior and the House.
Shield him and say nothing of the satchel.
Use him to feed the Confessor false word. *[Resolve 10]*

slots.plan: She eats only from his hand, the left. Maelis re-splints the leg with bad grace (she does not do dogs) and the bitch growls, not at people, at the floor: at the grate over the undercroft. Marrant's men bring the lymer up to the terrace wall below the kennels and she fights it through the bars until her mouth bleeds; the kennel-master wants her chained and Darrow sits with her instead. He names her Ash: for her colour, Hollis says, and because she is what is left when the fire is gone. She follows him up the ramp on three legs and lies down under his cot, where no lay brother will move her (ash_met; plan companion arrive ash).
slots.turn: By the end Darrow has a dog with a name under his cot and the kennel has told him where the cold is; he attempts to call her off the lymer and cannot, and names her instead

slots.plan: Wednesday's choice in its first clause: what became of the almoner. Then the cloister: two chairs, two wooden swords, and Hollis, who has thought for a fortnight about teaching the Captain to fight sitting down, does it: stop looking at the floor; the bind and the hold, a blade held is a blade not swinging; a one-legged man who learned it recently and badly, and a captain whose fingertips are still numb on the hilt. Wren as notary, the kitchen at the door. Darrow loses to a man with one leg and laughs for the first time since the river; Hollis's chair tips and he saves it with the sword, which is the lesson. Hollis names it on the page: the Seated Blade. Ends on the micro.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow can hold a stair from a chair, badly, with numb fingers, and the Art has its name on the page; he attempts to win and loses, and laughs

micro.ask: Hollis wants to be hit properly, not like a Mender. What does Darrow do?

slots.plan: The eve. Through Sister Pell's glass, banners on the Holloway below the Shins, a day off; and Marrant's camp striking its cart-canvas before dawn to go down and meet them: he will move first. Darrow sets the House's night with what he has: Wren to the tower with Pell, Hollis's chair at the tower door, Ash below the kennels, himself on the bell-tower stair with a chair and a stick; Maelis reads the Knots by lamplight and does not say the word. Wren refuses to be sent anywhere but the rope. Ends on the dusk bell, rung, and the lower terrace gone quiet under it.
slots.turn: By the end Darrow has placed every piece he has for a thing he cannot stand up for, and knows Marrant moves at dawn; he attempts to send Wren away from the tower and she refuses

world_moves: the grey cloaks' lymer was walked up to the terrace wall under the kennels and left tied there, baying at the kennel door through the night
the twenty riders under the banner that is not grey turned off the Holloway at the Wend landing and took the river road, a day further off than they should be
the House's letters did not go down this week: the almoner's satchel hung on its hook with nothing in it, and the winch-brothers sent the cage down empty

climax.plan: Old Mercy (arc b1.5), with Wednesday's choice and the week's tier deciding the almoner's fate as the arc fixes it. Marrant moves before the banners arrive: at dawn the cage rope is cut at the winch-house (the sixth man keeps it); the winter's salt and oil are already up, which only the kitchen's loaf-count explains, and in Triumph and Hard-won the tower's firewood came up by a second line nobody saw, hers. Marrant and four climb unarmed under the bell: Sister Pell is hurt, the bell falls silent, and sanctuary lapses at dusk unless it rings. Darrow holds the bell-tower stair seated (the Seated Blade, named Friday) while Wren climbs to ring; Hollis holds the tower door below from his chair; Ash holds the lymer at the terrace wall. Marrant, unarmed to the last, asks Maelis by a name that is not hers (T8); the censer's iron is the black of the sliver (T1). Rae, below, sees the rope fall and climbs the Steps in the dark, and is on the gate wall when the bell rings or does not. By tier: Triumph, the bell rings with light to spare and the grey cloaks go back down the Steps behind a Confessor who has stopped smiling; Hard-won, it rings on the last of the light, one of the four goes over the stair rail and lives, Marrant leaves with his writ and a limp; Costly, it rings a breath after dusk and only the Prior's reading of the law holds (the sun is down when the Prior says it is), and Marrant's writ gains a line against her; Setback, it rings with Marrant inside the tower, the law is argued not won, he goes down leaving a man and a paper and the Prior signs it to keep her roof. Ends on the choice; the Book's road is decided at this checkpoint (route decide --book 1) and the crossing follows his answer.
checks: might (the Seated Blade: holding the bell-tower stair seated against the first man up)
resolve (the Mender's Patience: the bell silent and the light going; fear and haste)
vigor (the hold on the stair until the bell rings; the bad hand)
insight (Warden's Eye: Marrant's lever: the name he asks the Mender by, and what he means to do with the almoner)
options: Go down to the lower terrace at dawn and tell Marrant, before his men, what the Reckoning showed him.
Let him go, and ring the bell for him as he leaves, as the law says.
Have Wren follow his camp down with a lamp and a knife, and the knife is not for show. *[Guile 4]*

quest_summary: Confessor Ivo Marrant is coming up the Holloway with five grey cloaks (six in all), a cart, a censer, and a writ naming the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's. Darrow's name is first; Hollis is second. Rae Thorne, the carter who heard the list read, is in the House; her cart and oxen wait at the winch-house below, where one of the six will stay; the rest camp on the lower terrace under the gate.
